svg.text: AdaptCPR wiring diagram (v0.6 - design only, not built yet)
Red wire = 24 V motor power. Blue wire = signal to the ESP32. Pins with a coloured dot and the same colour are joined together: black = GND (all one common ground), orange = 5 V, green = 3.3 V.
1. The E-stop has two contact sets: the power contact cuts 24 V to the motor directly (hardware, no software), the signal contact tells the ESP32.
2. The relay module in the parts list is NOT wired in this version. Decide later if you want it as a second cut-off.
3. The A3144 Hall sensors need 4.5 V or more, so they run on 5 V. Their pull-up goes to 3.3 V, so the ESP32 pin stays safe.
4. The INA219 is rated to 26 V and the supply is 24 V. That is close, so check the supply voltage with a meter before connecting it.
5. No custom PCB: everything uses ready-made boards. The ESP32 is powered from USB. Pins 34, 35, 36, 39 have no internal pull-up, so the 10k resistors are needed.
6. The buzzer on GPIO23 in the firmware is optional and is not in the parts list.
7. The motor encoder voltage (5 V here) is an assumption. Check the motor datasheet before powering it.
